_readme: Draft Oundle walk. [[c:...]] = cyan, not confirmed. Positions are guesses until recorded on site.
name: Back to the Market Place

layers.essential_history: [[c:Back where you started. Oundle has been a market town for over a thousand years.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:The Talbot's stories, from the Drumming Well to the Queen's staircase, are still told in the town today.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:The landlord, the mason, the carter, the schoolboy and Josiah Gant are all here. Time to say who took the crown.]]

directions_to_next: [[c:That's the end of the walk. Well done, detective!]]

puzzle.title: [[c:Who took the oak crown?]]
puzzle.intro: [[c:Look through your evidence notebook, then make your accusation.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Who took the crown, why, and where is it hidden?]]

fields.label: Why?
options: So his own inn would have the Queen's staircase story
To give it back to Fotheringhay
As a joke on the schoolboys
fields.answer: So his own inn would have the Queen's staircase story

hints: [[c:Whose story about being behind his bar didn't add up?]]
[[c:Whose handcart had a splinter of carved oak?]]
[[c:Where did Tom hear the footsteps going?]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:It was Josiah Gant. He wheeled the crown away on his handcart and hid it in the church tower, meaning to set it on his own staircase so travellers would stay at his inn instead of the Talbot. The crown goes back to the Talbot, and the Drumming Well falls silent.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:You can solve this from your notebook alone.]]
